key_insight: CatDiT uses a diffusion-transformer generative model in latent space to inverse-design heterogeneous catalysts with simultaneous control over adsorbate, binding energy, and catalyst class.
engineering_relevance: This provides a scalable way to rapidly screen and enrich catalyst candidates for reaction-specific targets, reducing reliance on exhaustive trial-and-error discovery.
method: Compress catalyst structures into latent representations for efficient training and sampling.
Condition generation on discrete and continuous properties at the same time.
Generate valid, novel candidates across intermetallic alloys and oxide surfaces.
evidence_signal: For nitrogen reduction reaction design, the model produced 28 DFT-relaxed alloy candidates within the target activity window and above the pure-metal *N-*H scaling line, giving about 1.5× enrichment over the source distribution.
watch_item: Performance depends on the quality and coverage of the latent training space, so generalization to less-represented catalyst chemistries may be limited.
paper_title: Catalyst Diffusion Transformer: Generative Inverse Design of Heterogeneous Catalysts
